info.title: Taskelith control-plane API
info.description: Login and sessions, projects with their members, defaults, auto-merge setting, and repository binding, the workers view, enrollment tokens, account slots, SCM integrations, and the webhook receiver (G3 item 9a); the board, task detail, and inbox views, inbox answers, agent sessions with their turns, native requests, responses, and output, and the server-sent event streams (G3 item 9b). A browser authenticates with the session cookie and sends the CSRF token on every mutation; the CLI and the owner use the operator credential. No response carries a stored secret; only issuing or rotating an enrollment token reveals its secret, once. The terminal WebSocket upgrade (G3 item 9d), whose frames `terminal.asyncapi.json` defines.

get.summary: Read the caller's session, starting an anonymous one when none is presented
get.description: Needs no credential. Without a valid session cookie it starts an anonymous server-side session, sets its cookie, and returns its CSRF token, which the login request needs.

Cache-Control.description: Always `no-store`, so that no cache keeps the response.

Set-Cookie.description: Present only when the request named no valid session: the cookie of the new anonymous session, with the attributes of the `browserSession` scheme.

500.description: The control plane failed; nothing is assumed to have taken effect.

503.description: A store the operation needs is unavailable; retry later.

post.summary: Log in with a login name and password
post.description: Authenticated by the anonymous session cookie and its CSRF token. On success the session gets a new identifier and a new CSRF token, so a session identifier known before the login is worthless after it.

Cache-Control.description: Always `no-store`, so that no cache keeps the response.

Set-Cookie.description: The session cookie `__Host-taskelith-session` with `HttpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Strict`, and `Path=/`, without `Domain`.

401.description: No anonymous session was presented (`unauthenticated`), or the login name and password do not match (`login-failed`).

403.description: The CSRF token is missing or wrong.

post.summary: Receive a webhook delivery of an SCM integration
post.description: Needs no session, CSRF token, or operator credential: the integration's plugin verifies the signature over the body bytes exactly as received, with the headers in lower case, before any payload is trusted (source control contract section 6). Redeliveries are deduplicated by the verified delivery identifier.

parameters.name: integrationId
parameters.description: The integration whose plugin verifies the delivery.

requestBody.description: The delivery body, read as bytes and never parsed before verification.

202.description: The delivery was verified and recorded, or it repeats a recorded delivery.

400.description: The delivery verified, but its plugin cannot parse the payload (`invalid`); nothing is recorded.

401.description: The integration is unknown, its identifier included, or the signature is missing or does not verify; the answer does not say which.

413.description: The body exceeds the receiver's limit.

parameters.description: The `id` of the last event the client received, which a browser sends when it reconnects; it wins over `after`.

200.description: A `text/event-stream` of events in position order, each a frame with `id`, `event`, and one `data` line of JSON, except `resync` and `stream-ended`, whose frames have no `id`; comment lines keep the connection alive and carry no event.

Cache-Control.description: Always `no-store`, so that no cache keeps the stream.

401.description: No valid session cookie or operator credential was presented.

403.description: The principal lacks the required role.

500.description: The control plane failed; nothing is assumed to have taken effect.

503.description: A store the operation needs is unavailable; retry later.

get.summary: Open or reattach the terminal of a session's active attempt as a WebSocket
get.description: Requires `project-operator` or above on the project; an `installation-owner` needs a project role. The control plane authenticates, checks the `Origin` of a session-authenticated upgrade, and checks the role before it reads the session. A browser cannot send the CSRF header on a WebSocket handshake, so a cookie-authenticated connection sends its CSRF token in its first frame, `terminal.attach`.

parameters.name: attemptId
parameters.description: The session's active bound attempt, as the caller read it.

parameters.name: ownershipGeneration
parameters.description: The attempt's ownership generation, as the caller read it.

parameters.name: generation
parameters.description: The session's running generation, as the caller read it.

parameters.name: Sec-WebSocket-Key
parameters.description: The client's handshake nonce, 16 random bytes in base64.

parameters.name: Sec-WebSocket-Protocol
parameters.description: The subprotocols the client offers, a comma-separated list that must include `taskelith.terminal.v1`; the 101 answer selects it.

parameters.name: Origin
parameters.description: The page's origin, which a browser always sends; a session-authenticated upgrade without it, or from another origin than the installation's, is refused with 403 `csrf-token-invalid`.

101.description: Switching Protocols: the connection is a WebSocket that carries the frames of `terminal.asyncapi.json`.

400.description: A path or query parameter or a handshake header is invalid.

401.description: No valid session cookie or operator credential was presented.

403.description: The principal lacks the required role (`role-required`), or a session-authenticated upgrade came from another origin (`csrf-token-invalid`).

404.description: No such agent session in the project.

422.description: The attempt is not current, or no terminal is offered.

500.description: The control plane failed; nothing is assumed to have taken effect.

503.description: A store the operation needs is unavailable, or the worker's relay connection is not open; retry later.

Failure.description: A kernel failure: callers branch on the code, never on the message.

Identifier.description: An opaque identifier of 1-128 printable ASCII characters without whitespace.

Instant.description: A UTC time in the form YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ.

DisplayText.description: Text shown to people and never interpreted, without control characters.

Generation.description: A compare-and-set generation that starts at 1.

oneOf.description: The check failed; each detail is a problem.
The check does not apply at this start; the one detail is the reason.

SelfCheckId.description: A worker admission check: 1-64 lowercase letters, digits, and '-', starting with a letter.

NotApplicableReason.description: Why a check does not apply at this start, derived on the worker from its platform and launch settings.

AuthenticationFailure.description: Status 401: `unauthenticated` when no valid session cookie or operator credential was presented, `login-failed` when a login name and password do not match, without saying which.

AccessDenial.description: Status 403: the authenticated principal lacks the role the operation requires.

CsrfRejection.description: Status 403: a mutation authenticated by the session cookie carried no `X-CSRF-Token` header, or one that is not its session's token; nothing took effect.

WebhookRejection.description: Status 401 of the webhook receiver: an unknown integration or a missing or failed signature, with one body that does not say which.

CsrfToken.description: The CSRF token of the caller's server-side session: 256 random bits in base64url. It authenticates nothing without the session cookie; the client sends it in the `X-CSRF-Token` header of every mutation.

LoginName.description: The name a principal logs in with: 1-64 lowercase letters, digits, '.', '_', or '-', starting with a letter or digit.

Password.description: A login password. Write-only: no response, log, or failure carries it; item 10 sets the password policy.

Principal.description: An operator principal of the Access module.

AnonymousSession.description: A server-side session before login; its CSRF token protects the login request.

expiresAt.description: When the server-side session ends unless it is renewed; item 10 sets the lifetime.

next.description: The identifier to pass as `after` for the next page; absent on the last page.

pluginId.description: The SDLC framework plugin that new runs of the project bind to; the version is fixed at binding.

SpecApprover.description: Who approves a task's specification by default (product ports section 6.1).

NoEligibleSlotPolicy.description: What a new session does when its pool has no eligible slot (account pool contract section 4.5).

HarnessPreference.description: Harness plugin identifiers in the project's order of preference: the first is the default implementer, and the rest are tried in order after a limit (account pool contract section 4.4).

changedBy.description: The principal of the last change; absent until the first change after creation.

next.description: The identifier to pass as `after` for the next page; absent on the last page.

AutoMergeSetting.description: The project's auto-merge setting (product ports section 6.2).

changedBy.description: The maintainer of the last change; absent until the first change.

ExternalId.description: An identifier that an external service issues, compared exactly and never parsed (source control contract section 2, rule 3).

BranchName.description: A branch name that `git check-ref-format --branch` accepts, non-ASCII letters included: no control character, space, '~', '^', ':', '?', '*', '[', or '\'; no '..', '@{', or '//'; no component that starts with '.' or ends with '.lock'; not starting with '-' or '/', not ending with '/' or '.', and not 'HEAD'. Git sets no length limit; at most 1024 characters only bound the request, as `ExternalId` does.

RemoteUrl.description: A bound remote URL: HTTPS with a host name and an optional port from 1 to 65535, without IPv6 literal, user information, query, or fragment, which a workspace clones from and pushes to (git workspace contract sections 3 and 7), so that no secret can be part of it. Its origin is the allowed origin of the binding's SCM integration when it was bound.

RemoteUrlCandidate.description: A remote URL that `bindRepository` checks: an absolute URL with an authority and no white space. A URL that is not HTTPS, holds user information, a query, or a fragment, or whose normalized origin is not the integration's allowed origin is refused with 422 `BindingRefusal`.

AllowedOrigin.description: The origin that the integration's remote URLs must have: the scheme https, a host name, and an optional port from 1 to 65535, with no IPv6 literal, user information, path, query, or fragment. Only an `installation-owner` sets it. The control plane stores it normalized as `NormalizedOrigin`.

NormalizedOrigin.description: An origin after normalization: scheme and host in lower case and the port explicit, 443 when none was given. Origins are compared only in this form.

BindingRefusal.description: Status 422 of `bindRepository`, checked in this order: the remote URL is not HTTPS, holds user information, a query, or a fragment, or its normalized origin is not the integration's allowed origin; or the integration's plugin does not declare the merge method in its `SourceControlCapabilities`.

integrationId.description: The SCM integration that serves the repository.

integrationBranch.description: The target branch of the project's merges (product ports section 6.3) and the base branch of its workspaces (git workspace contract section 3).

expectedRevision.description: Required when the project is bound; absent for the first binding.

reportedAt.description: When the last report was consumed; absent before the first.

results.description: The stored results, in check identifier order.

WorkersView.description: The workers view (worker admission contract section 8); it holds no credential or credential hash.

workers.description: Every enrolled worker that is not revoked, in identifier order; never partial.

HostConstraints.description: What an enrollment token binds the enrolling host to; an absent field accepts any host.

EnrollmentToken.description: An unused enrollment token; never its secret.

EnrollmentTokenPage.description: Pending tokens (unused, unexpired, and not revoked) in identifier order.

next.description: The identifier to pass as `after` for the next page; absent on the last page.

EnrollmentTokenSecret.description: The single-use enrollment token: `tken_` and 256 random bits in base64url (installation contract section 5).

IssuedEnrollmentToken.description: The one response that reveals a token's secret; only its hash is stored, so it cannot be read again.

ConcurrencyLimit.description: Concurrent held reservations of a slot.

SlotCredential.description: A slot credential. Write-only: stored encrypted and revealed only to the run that reserved the slot, never in a response.

AccountSlot.description: A slot record without its credential (account pool contract section 3.1).

next.description: The identifier to pass as `after` for the next page; absent on the last page.

ProjectAccountSlot.description: An active slot of the project's pools, as a project member sees it.

sharedWithOtherProjects.description: Whether the slot also serves other projects, which are never named.

ProjectAccountSlotPage.description: The project's pool slots in identifier order.

next.description: The identifier to pass as `after` for the next page; absent on the last page.

SettingName.description: A setting or secret name that the SCM plugin defines.

ScmSettings.description: Non-secret settings that the SCM plugin defines and checks.

ScmSecrets.description: Secret values that the SCM plugin defines, such as its signing key and webhook secret. Write-only: stored encrypted, never returned.

secretNames.description: The names of the stored secrets, never their values.

next.description: The identifier to pass as `after` for the next page; absent on the last page.

allowedOrigin.description: Replaces the allowed origin; the next credential issue for each binding re-checks it.

secrets.description: Replaces the named secrets and keeps the others.

AttemptOutcome.description: How the attempt ended. It does not accept the task's work.

cancelled.description: Whether cancellation was requested before the attempt ended.
Whether cancellation was requested before the attempt ended.
Whether cancellation was requested before the attempt ended.

ExitStatus.description: An exit code, a terminating signal, or an unknown status.

ContentDigest.description: sha256: followed by 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters.

EventPosition.description: A position of the control-plane event stream, a decimal integer of at most 16 digits: `0` before any event, and each event's position greater than every earlier committed event's. A position exists only once the change it reports has committed.

ViewStamp.description: The time of a view's state and the event stream position it reflects (product ports section 2, rule 2).

IdempotencyKey.description: A client's key that makes a command safe to repeat: the same key with the same input returns the first outcome, and with other input fails with `conflict` (product ports section 2, rule 7).

AgentSessionId.description: A session of the session timeline (`SessionId`), one task's agent session; not a login session.

AgentSessionGeneration.description: A generation of an agent session, one native process, from 1 (`SessionGeneration`).

NativeRequestId.description: The opaque native request ID that the harness port returned.

TimelinePosition.description: A position in one of a session's ordered lists (turns, native requests, or output), from 1 without gaps.

TimelineCursor.description: `0` before the first entry, or the position of the last entry the reader holds.

HarnessText.description: Text of a native request, an output entry, or an answer, at most 65,536 characters (`MAX_HARNESS_TEXT_LENGTH`).

TurnState.description: A turn's state (session timeline contract section 4.3).

NativeRequestState.description: A native request's state (session timeline contract section 5.5).

DeliveryState.description: The delivery of a consumed response (session timeline contract section 5.4).

DelegationResultOutcome.description: A delegated child's outcome in a delegation result (`DELEGATION_OUTCOMES`).

NativeRequestKey.description: A native request's identity within its session: its generation and native request ID (`RequestKey`).

BoardColumn.description: A board column (`BOARD_COLUMNS`, product ports section 3.1).

MergeGateState.description: The merge gate on the board (`MERGE_GATE_STATES`, product ports section 3.4).

CardWait.description: Why a card does not move (`CARD_WAIT_KINDS`).

EvidenceKind.description: The evidence kind a gate requires (`EVIDENCE_KINDS`).

EvidenceFreshness.description: The freshness of a requirement's evidence (`EVIDENCE_FRESHNESS`).

TaskEndKind.description: Why a task ended without a merge (`TASK_END_KINDS`, product ports section 3.9).

SessionActivity.description: The activity of a task's agent session (product ports section 3.6); `none` without a session.

StageSummary.description: A card's current stage (product ports section 3.2).

FrameworkVersion.description: The run binding's SDLC framework plugin and version.

PlacementObstacle.description: Why a task is not placed (product ports section 3.8); `observedAt` is when its source observed it.

TaskEnd.description: A task that ended without a merge and that only a re-admission resumes (product ports section 3.9).

BoardCard.description: One root workflow run, keyed by `runId` (product ports section 3.3).

needsYou.description: Open inbox items of the card: its run's tasks and their delegated child tasks.

Board.description: The project board (product ports section 3.5), one snapshot.

cards.description: Every card of the project; never partial.

TraceLink.description: A requirement's native reference with its work items, attempts, and evidence freshness.

dispatchedGeneration.description: The ownership generation the admission's dispatch started, not the task's current one.

TaskView.description: A G2 task of the card's run, or a delegated child of one of them.

taskRunId.description: The task's own run: a child run for a delegated task, never the card's key.

TaskDetail.description: The task detail of one card (product ports section 3.7), one snapshot.

stages.description: The run's stages in graph order.

tasks.description: Every task of the run and every delegated child task of its lineage, in admission order.

InboxItemKind.description: An inbox item's kind (`NEEDS_YOU_KINDS`, product ports section 4.1).

AnsweringRole.description: The least human role that may answer an item (`ANSWERING_ROLES`).

InboxSubject.description: What an item waits on: a card, or a worker's process outside any project. An item about a native request names it by `sessionId`, `sessionGeneration`, and `nativeRequestId` (`NativeRequestInboxSubject`).

NativeRequestInboxSubject.description: The card subject of a `permission-request`, `input-request`, or `delivery-acknowledgement` item: its native request is the request of `sessionId` whose key is `sessionGeneration` and `nativeRequestId`, because a later generation can reuse a native request ID (session timeline contract section 5.3).

InboxAnswer.description: An answer of the item's kind (product ports section 4.1).

InputAnswerText.description: The text of an input answer, at most `MAX_INPUT_ANSWER_BYTES`, 65,536 bytes in UTF-8, through the inbox or the session; a text within that bound is also within `MAX_HARNESS_TEXT_LENGTH`, which counts UTF-16 code units.

InboxItemStatus.description: `open`; `resolved` with its resolver, time, and answer; or `closed` when its subject stopped waiting on a person without an answer.

InboxItem.description: One item that waits on a person (product ports section 4.1). Only an `escalation` item carries an escalation reason, and only a `reconciliation` item a reconciliation reason.

InboxView.description: A scope's open inbox items, one snapshot.

items.description: The scope's open items, newest first; never partial.

InboxCounts.description: A scope's open item counts, one snapshot.

byCard.description: Per card with open items; empty for the installation scope.

CommandConflict.description: Status 409: the item or request already holds another answer (`already-answered`), or the idempotency key was used before with other input (`idempotency-key-reused`); nothing changed.

AnswerRefusal.description: Status 422: the item is closed (`item-closed`); the attempt or its generation that the item or response names is no longer the current one (`attempt-not-current`); or the subject's state no longer allows the answer (`subject-changed`), which the command rechecks in its own transaction; nothing changed.

TurnAuthor.description: A person, or the host with the delegation request whose child's outcome the turn delivers (session timeline contract section 4.1).

Turn.description: A turn with its immutable identity and its progress; a failure is present exactly when the outcome is `failed`.

PersonAnswer.description: An answer a person gives to a permission or input request.

NativeAnswer.description: A consumed answer: a person's or a standing rule's permission answer, a person's input answer, or the host's delegation result (session timeline contract section 5.2).

Responder.description: Who gave a consumed answer: a person, a standing rule, or the host.

NativeRequest.description: A recorded native request; `position` is its place in the session's recording order. An answered request carries its consumed response.

OutputEntry.description: One retained output entry; an empty output records none.

AgentSessionHandoff.description: The host-written handoff of a session stopped by a limit (session timeline contract section 8).

runId.description: The card the task belongs to.

limit.description: Present once an account limit stopped the session, which then accepts no new attempt, turn, delivery, or generation; with the reset time when a signal carried it.

output.description: The retained output window: the position of its earliest entry, absent while it holds none, and the last position ever taken.

AgentSessionPage.description: Agent sessions of a card's tasks in identifier order.

next.description: The identifier to pass as `after` for the next page; absent on the last page.
The position to pass as `after` for the next page; absent on the last page.
The position to pass as `after` for the next page; absent on the last page.

OutputRead.description: Retained output after the cursor, or `cursor-expired` with the earliest retained position when the cursor left the window (session timeline contract section 7); the reader then falls back to a snapshot.

next.description: The position to pass as `after` for the next page; absent on the last page.

TurnRefusal.description: Status 422 of `submitTurn`: the session is stopped by an account limit, so its task's next session takes the work; nothing changed.

ResponseRefusal.description: Status 422 of `respondToNativeRequest`: the attempt or ownership generation it names is not the session's active bound one; nothing changed.

NativeResponseSubmission.description: A person's response to a native request, naming the attempt and ownership generation it answers for.

BoardChangedEvent.description: The number of workers online changed, also on a board with no cards; `workersOnline` as `readBoard` returns it at this event.

CardChangedEvent.description: A card or its task detail changed; the card as of this event.

InboxItemChangedEvent.description: An inbox item opened, was resolved, or closed; the item as of this event. When the item counts toward a card, the same change also sends that card's `card-changed` event with its new `needsYou`.

AgentSessionChangedEvent.description: An agent session was opened or bound an attempt, a generation started or ended, it stopped, or its handoff was written or taken.

TurnChangedEvent.description: A turn was recorded or changed state.

NativeRequestChangedEvent.description: A native request was recorded, answered, expired, or became unresolved, or its delivery was reported.

ResyncEvent.description: The stream cannot resume after the cursor: it is below the stream's retention floor (`cursor-expired`), or beyond the head of the installation-wide sequence (`cursor-unknown`). The frame has no `id`, and the server ends the stream after it; the client closes its `EventSource`, reads its views again, and opens a new stream after their positions.

StreamEndedEvent.description: The server ends the stream because the principal's roles changed (`role-changed`), raised or lowered. The frame has no `id`; the client reads its views again and reconnects with its `Last-Event-ID`, which the server authorizes anew.

ProjectEvent.description: The `data` of one event of a project stream, as JSON; the frame's `event` field is its `type`, and its `id` field its `position`, except for `resync` and `stream-ended`, whose frames have no `id`.

InstallationEvent.description: The `data` of one event of the installation stream, as JSON; the frame's `event` field is its `type`, and its `id` field its `position`, except for `resync` and `stream-ended`, whose frames have no `id`.

TerminalRefusal.description: Status 422 of `openTerminal`, checked in this order: `attempt-not-current` when the attempt, its ownership generation, or the session generation that the request names is not the session's active bound attempt and running generation; `terminal-not-offered` when the session's harness declares no terminal, the worker runs on macOS, or the worker's common protocol version is below 2. Nothing was opened.

browserSession.name: __Host-taskelith-session
browserSession.description: The server-side session identifier, 256 random bits, in a cookie set with `HttpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Strict`, and `Path=/`, without `Domain`. The `__Host-` prefix makes the browser refuse the cookie without `Secure` and `Path=/` or with `Domain`; `HttpOnly` and `SameSite=Strict` rest on the server alone. Never readable by scripts and never in a response body.

csrfToken.name: X-CSRF-Token
csrfToken.description: The CSRF token of the session that the cookie names, required with the cookie on every operation other than GET; compared in constant time.
